content.value_statement: Google Workspace CLI users need consistent authentication, flags, and shell quoting guidance. This skill provides a shared reference for safe gws command planning across supported agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains the gws binary prerequisite and authentication options.
Documents global flags for format, dry run, and sanitization.
Shows the common gws command structure for services and resources.
Lists method flags for parameters, request bodies, file paths, uploads, and pagination.
Provides safety rules for secrets and write or delete confirmation.
Gives shell quoting tips for zsh ranges and structured values.
limitations: Does not install the gws binary or verify the local environment.
Does not complete OAuth or service account setup for the user.
Does not document every Google Workspace service or method.
Requires the user to manage credentials, permissions, and API access.

use_cases.title: Prepare CLI Authentication
use_cases.description: Review OAuth and service account setup before running Google Workspace commands.

use_cases.title: Plan Safe Workspace Changes
use_cases.description: Use dry runs, confirmations, and output formats before write or delete operations.

use_cases.title: Fix Shell Quoting Issues
use_cases.description: Choose safe quoting for sheet ranges, parameters, and structured command values.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my environment is ready for gws. Explain required authentication choices and ask before running any command.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Output Format
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a read-only gws command. Recommend an output format and explain when to use dry run.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Safe Write
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a gws write operation for review. Include required flags, a dry-run step, and a confirmation checkpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Design Paginated Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a paginated gws export with safe delays, output handling, and sanitization. Explain credential and PII precautions.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to authenticate before using gws.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains browser OAuth and service account options, then asks which account type the user wants to use.

output_examples.input: A user needs to list Drive files with a small page size.
output: The assistant identifies the Drive files list method.
It recommends query parameters and a readable output format.
It reminds the user not to print secrets.

output_examples.input: A user requests a destructive update.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a dry run first and asks for confirmation before any write or delete command.

best_practices: Confirm user intent before write or delete commands.
Use dry run when testing destructive or data-changing operations.
Keep credential file paths local and never print token contents.
anti_patterns: Running write or delete commands without explicit confirmation.
Sharing API keys, tokens, or service account key contents in chat.
Treating repository stars or issue comments as required workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It provides shared gws CLI guidance for authentication, flags, output formats, and shell quoting.

faq.question: Does it install gws?
faq.answer: No. The gws binary must already be installed and available on the system path.

faq.question: Can it authenticate me automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains OAuth and service account patterns, but users must complete authentication steps.

faq.question: Does it call Google APIs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is reference material. Commands should run only after user approval.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Keep credential files private, avoid printing secrets, and use only the permissions needed.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
